about: Archived risk inventory; retained findings are consolidated during Phase 1.

severity_scale.critical: customer data or an unauthorised consequential action is reachable; blocks any production use
severity_scale.high: a stated control does not hold in some real deployment shape; blocks the first customer workflow
severity_scale.medium: degrades evidence quality or operability; must be closed before general availability
severity_scale.low: known limitation with a documented workaround

risks.title: Metric cardinality repaired; multiprocess aggregation and soak unverified
risks.description: HTTP metrics use matched route templates and a fixed unmatched bucket. The registry bounds series globally, excludes tenant/agent labels, escapes values, serializes concurrent updates and emits cumulative duration buckets. Registry state remains process-local.
risks.impact: Prometheus cardinality grows with traffic; the /metrics response grows without bound in the same process.
risks.mitigation: Use one API process per pod and scrape each pod separately for candidate validation. Do not infer deployment-wide values from a load-balanced multiprocess metrics endpoint.
risks.closing_evidence: Exact-release tests in tests_arch/test_observability_bounds.py, a real per-pod scrape and aggregation test, and bounded-memory soak on the declared topology.
risks.reproduction: Send 10,000 different unknown request paths and concurrently record/scrape metrics; then compare separate worker counters with the intended deployment aggregate.
risks.root_cause: Raw path labels created one series per supplied identifier, histograms lacked buckets, and counters were process-local.

risks.title: Automatic reconciliation covers Kubernetes, GitHub contents and brokered AWS; the rest needs a human
risks.description: A definitive 4xx from the target is now a recorded FAILED operation, not an unknown one. A lost response or 5xx stays unknown, and for the Kubernetes tool the maintenance loop asks the target: this operation's field manager present means succeeded, the approved resourceVersion unchanged after a 120-second quiescence window means failed, anything else stays unknown. It never writes, needs evidence for every verdict and stops after SENTINEL_RECONCILE_MAX_ATTEMPTS. Proven against a fake API at every boundary and against a real local Kubernetes 1.37 API server. Other tools (AWS, GitHub, PostgreSQL, HTTP) have no reconciler and still need a human. Deletes are settled by end state and the deleting actor is not attributed. On 2026-09-20 GitHub contents writes and deletes gained a reconciler based on the git blob sha (not attributed), GitHub and AWS 4xx responses stopped being recorded as succeeded operations, and the read-only SQL adapter can no longer leave an unknown outcome. GitHub POSTs, other GitHub PUTs and every AWS mutation still need a human. Later on 2026-09-20 AWS operations run under a brokered role session gained a CloudTrail reconciler keyed on the session name: an event without an errorCode is succeeded, with one is failed, and no event stays unknown because delivery lags and only management events are recorded. It is tested against a fake only; it has never queried a real CloudTrail.
risks.impact: A remote change can succeed despite a timeout. Operators must reconcile against the target before retrying; a consumed authorization does not prove the remote effect occurred exactly once.
risks.mitigation: Automatic target lookup for Kubernetes; explicit state, error log and console list for everything it cannot settle.
risks.closing_evidence: The reconcilers exercised against the real services used in a customer's first workflow, plus observed settlement times from a paid pilot in GET /v1/workflow/metrics
risks.reproduction: Inspect the stated evidence gap and rerun the acceptance check described in closing_evidence; no production observation is asserted.
risks.root_cause: Invoked-target errors and post-effect bookkeeping failures are now reported as unknown_after_effect immediately when storage is available; otherwise the durable pending intent remains for deadline reconciliation. Counted effects and tenant isolation passed local HTTP tests on SQLite and PostgreSQL. Automatic Kubernetes target verification is absent.
risks.acceptance_criteria: The reconcilers exercised against the real services used in a customer's first workflow, plus observed settlement times from a paid pilot in GET /v1/workflow/metrics

risks.title: Final image inherits unresolved high-severity OS advisories
risks.description: The Debian-based image carried 44 HIGH findings with no fixed version. The runtime moved to a digest-pinned Wolfi base with Python 3.12 and libstdc++ only; dependencies are installed with --require-hashes into a virtualenv in the builder, so the runtime has no pip, compiler or package cache. On 2026-09-20 a local build served /health/ready as uid 10001 after migrating to schema 37, and Trivy (vuln, secret, misconfig; HIGH,CRITICAL) reported 0 findings, judged PASS by scripts/build_and_scan_image.py. This is one local scan on one date. CI has not run it, no image has been published or signed, and a base pinned by digest stops receiving fixes until it is moved.
risks.impact: The vulnerability release gate is not satisfied; no production release is authorized by the local functional tests.
risks.mitigation: Minimal base, no package manager tooling in the runtime, fail-closed gate on every HIGH/CRITICAL finding including unfixed ones.
risks.closing_evidence: The docker CI job passing the same gate on the release commit, the published image digest signed and verified, and a scheduled rescan with an owner for moving the base digest
risks.affected_surface: Container base and runtime OS packages
risks.reproduction: Run Trivy vuln scan for HIGH,CRITICAL against the recorded local image ID using the dated database; retain full JSON and tool version.
risks.root_cause: Inherited distribution advisories have no packaged fixes in this scan. The historical unfixed exemption in local/CI release gates has now been removed.
risks.release_status: OPEN; no suppressions or accepted exceptions
risks.customer_impact: Unresolved image vulnerability posture prevents the declared production acceptance.
risks.rollback_plan: Keep enforcement onboarding paused; preserve evidence and data. Do not select an older artifact without scanning it; redeploy only a reviewed artifact/configuration pair.

risks.title: Workload identity is implemented but off by default and no customer issuer is integrated
risks.description: SPIFFE JWT-SVIDs and pod-bound Kubernetes tokens are verified, and SENTINEL_REQUIRE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY refuses API keys on the agent path. Keys may be pinned or fetched from a stated https jwks_uri: refreshed on a schedule and, rate-limited, when an unseen key id appears; a failed or hostile response keeps the last good keys. A projected pod-bound token from a real agent pod was accepted by deployed Sentinel pods on a local cluster. OIDC discovery is supported (the document must name exactly the registered issuer), which is how SPIRE's OIDC Discovery Provider, Okta and Entra are consumed. Tenants first seen in a verified human sign-in are now enrolled. Still missing: a SPIRE Workload API client, a Kubernetes API server JWKS fetch (needs a credential and the cluster CA), and any customer issuer. The default is false (DECISION_LOG FCX-006).
risks.impact: Until a deployment turns the requirement on, any holder of a tenant API key can name any agent.
risks.mitigation: The requirement exists and is tested; the agent id is bound to the credential for every IdP-issued token regardless of the setting.
risks.closing_evidence: A design partner running with SENTINEL_REQUIRE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY=true against their issuer for the pilot window, including one issuer key rotation

risks.root_cause: SPIFFE JWT-SVIDs and pod-bound Kubernetes service-account tokens are verified against keys supplied at registration, and SENTINEL_REQUIRE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY refuses API keys on the agent path. The default is false (DECISION_LOG FCX-006) because turning it on needs the customer's issuer. Keys are static: there is no JWKS fetch, no SPIRE Workload API client and no rotation without a configuration change. The only issuer exercised is a local kind cluster's.

risks.title: Bypass prevention is proven on two clusters and two network plugins, for Kubernetes only
risks.description: deploy/protected-changes ships a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (failurePolicy Fail, Kubernetes 1.30 or later) that refuses writes by agent service accounts and unstamped writes or deletes by the executor. Deletes are now stamped on the object before deletion, closing the earlier DELETE exemption. scripts/run_deployed_journey.py showed, on a one-node local cluster with kindnet, the API server refusing both bypass attempts and the CNI blocking an agent pod from the API server and the internet. Human users and other controllers are out of scope by design. Nothing equivalent exists for AWS, GitHub or databases, and no other CNI or cloud cluster was exercised. AWS and GitHub now have per-operation constrained credentials (a fifteen-minute role session; a per-call App installation token scoped to one repository and permission family) but no target-side control that refuses changes made around Sentinel, and those paths are tested against fakes only. The deployed journey now runs over TLS under a private CA; mutual TLS and rotation are not exercised. The same refusals held on AWS under k3s with flannel and kube-router on 2026-09-20.
risks.impact: In a cluster without the policy applied, or for a non-Kubernetes target, an agent holding a write credential can act without Sentinel and Sentinel's evidence is true and incomplete.
risks.mitigation: Coverage reports observed versus routed separately; the admission policy and RBAC are shipped and structurally tested.
risks.closing_evidence: The policy and the egress NetworkPolicy applied in a customer cluster on their CNI, with a recorded bypass attempt from an agent pod refused at both layers
risks.reproduction: Rerun the acceptance check named in closing_evidence against the exact release; no production observation is asserted.
risks.root_cause: deploy/protected-changes ships a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy that refuses writes by agent service accounts and unstamped writes by the executor, with failurePolicy Fail. It was exercised against a local Kubernetes 1.37 API server. It requires Kubernetes 1.30 or later. DELETE carries no field manager, so executor deletes are constrained by RBAC and preconditions only. Human users and other controllers are out of scope by design. Network egress enforcement depends on the customer's CNI and was not exercised. Nothing equivalent exists for AWS, GitHub or databases.

risks.title: The transparency log was empty until migration 37 and is still not anchored outside the environment
risks.description: Before 2026-09-20 nothing in the running service appended to the transparency log. Receipts are now committed by the maintenance loop and export as a bundle that verifies offline. standard/execution-passport-v1/witness_root.py lets a customer record roots on a machine the operator does not control, verifying locally that each root is a consistent extension of the last; tests show it refusing a rewritten and a truncated log, and a drill restores evidence into a new database and verifies an old bundle against the customer-held root. What is missing is a customer actually running the witness, and publication to an object-lock sink in a second failure domain. Evidence bodies are now sealed per record when a data key is configured, and production refuses to start without a key or an explicit opt-out; keys come from the environment or a Kubernetes secret rather than a KMS, and key loss loses bodies (never digests or proofs).
risks.impact: An operator who controls the database can still rewrite the whole log undetected unless the customer holds earlier roots.
risks.mitigation: Offline verifier with a trusted-root check; the export states whether any root was ever anchored; R-003 tracks independent recovery.
risks.closing_evidence: A design partner's scheduled witness file covering the pilot window, and a drill in a second failure domain that verifies an old bundle against it (see R-003)
risks.reproduction: Rerun the acceptance check named in closing_evidence against the exact release; no production observation is asserted.
risks.root_cause: Before 2026-09-20 nothing in the running service appended to the transparency log, so roots and proofs were served over an empty tree. Receipts are now committed by the maintenance loop (exactly once, asynchronously) and export as a bundle that verifies offline. A bundle proves membership in a root; it proves history only against a root held outside the environment. Publication to an object-lock sink exists and is optional; no deployment has published one, and no restore in an independent failure domain has verified old evidence with separately held roots.

risks.title: Throughput is measured on one machine with one service process
risks.description: scripts/run_workflow_loadtest.py drives evaluate plus bound execute against a real uvicorn process and PostgreSQL with a no-op tool. On 2026-09-20 on an arm64 macOS laptop it completed 2,000 changes with no failure at about 175 changes per second with 16 concurrent clients (evaluate p95 42 ms, execute p95 67 ms). Client, service and database shared the machine; there was no network, no TLS, one process and no replica contention, and rate limits were raised so they would not shape the result.
risks.impact: No sizing or capacity statement can be made to a customer; the figure is a regression baseline.
risks.mitigation: The report carries its environment and limitations and must never be quoted without them.
risks.closing_evidence: The same workload on the supported topology (multiple replicas, managed PostgreSQL, TLS) with the customer's expected concurrency, bound to the release commit

risks.title: GitHub App constrained credentials have never met the real service
risks.description: AWS half CLOSED on 2026-09-25: a real AssumeRole per operation under the operation's session name, the operation signed with the temporary credential, and CloudTrail LookupEvents settling the outcome (archive/pre-cleanup:scripts/run_aws_sts_proof.py; two signer defects found and fixed on the way: NAT64 addresses and the us-east-1 scope of global endpoints). GitHub half OPEN: the App assertion and scoped installation-token request have still met only fakes.
risks.impact: The first real use may be refused by the vendor, or a CloudTrail lookup may never match and leave every AWS unknown outcome for a human. A refusal is a known absence, so the failure is safe; it is not useful.
risks.mitigation: Refusals at every step are recorded as not attempted; no credential reaches a result; the AWS path is now proven against the real service.
risks.closing_evidence: One recorded run of the GitHub App path against a test installation, bound to the release commit
risks.root_cause: STS AssumeRole with a per-operation session name, CloudTrail LookupEvents by that name, the GitHub App assertion and the scoped installation-token request are implemented from the vendors' documented contracts and tested against fakes that encode that reading. No request has been sent to AWS or GitHub. Signature scope for the global STS endpoint, the exact LookupEvents attribute that carries an assumed-role session, permission-family names and error shapes are the places such a reading is usually wrong.

risks.title: MCP streaming relay has met no third-party server and has no concurrency measurement
risks.description: Guarded incremental relay of MCP notifications is implemented and tested against scripted upstreams only. No third-party MCP server has been proxied with streaming on. Each streamed call holds one worker thread for its duration (up to 120 s), and no measurement exists of how many concurrent streams a replica sustains. Servers that depend on sampling, elicitation or the standalone GET stream do not work through the proxy, by design.
risks.impact: A real server's event framing or notification shapes may be dropped rather than relayed, which is safe but not useful; many long streams could exhaust the worker pool of a replica that enables the setting.
risks.mitigation: Off by default. Per-event, total-size and wall-time bounds; dropped messages are counted in the audit row; the final result path is unchanged.
risks.closing_evidence: A recorded run with streaming on against at least two independently implemented MCP servers, and a load measurement of concurrent streams per replica, bound to the release commit
